articles.title: Eagles rumors: Landon Dickerson has drawn interest on trade market
articles.summary: As the 2026 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaches, fans of the Philadelphia Eagles have thoroughly discussed who should or shouldn’t be traded now that a pla...
articles.body:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaches, fans of the Philadelphia Eagles have thoroughly discussed who should or shouldn't be traded now that a playoff berth is all but out of reach.

With Cam Jurgens already gone , should the 2-6 Eagles approach the rare opportunity to load up on picks in an otherwise lost season with gusto, saying goodbye to more members of their Super Bowl core to try to build a new one? Or would it be better to hold onto Moro Ojomo and Riq Woolen now in the hopes of bringing them back in 2027, even if that would create more cap issues, instead of alleviating them?

While that opinion depends on the individual, on ESPN's The Aftermath, Adam Schefter revealed another Eagles stalwart on a long-term contract that other teams have inquired about: Landon Dickerson .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Then a couple of other teams that have really struggled, obviously, the Philadelphia Eagles are one," Schefter wrote. "I know they have some veterans on expiring contracts that teams would consider. Riq Wollin would be the kind of guy. Landon Dickerson, I know some teams have been interested in."

Ironically enough, Dickerson actually commented on the potential of being traded in an appearance on 94WIP, explaining that, at this point, trade conversations are part of the game, but he does love playing in Philadelphia and wouldn't mind being a one-team guy for his career .

"I mean, the thing is, the longer that you kind of stay in this professional athlete field, you do realize that there's really two sides to every organization. There's coaches and football players, and then there's front office stuff. I'm worried about playing football, and you just kind of have to come to accept that the trade stuff and everything, that's just part of the job," Dickerson said.

"When it comes to being in this career, in this profession is the trade stuff and all that stuff is, it's something you really, you can't focus on and worry about. And I feel the same way about it. I love this city. This right now is my home. I spend offseasons here. I love my teammates, coaches. I love everybody. And I really don't want to play for another team, but at the same time, again, that's not a decision that when it comes to trade stuff, you can make as a player, you don't just get to say, 'Well, I like being here, so don't trade me.'"

If a team came calling and would be willing to give up a solid pick for Dickerson, would Howie Roseman actually say no? Dickerson has spent much of the last two years dealing with injuries, and with his contract running through 2028 – with additional void years going through 2032 – if a team is willing to give up a pick for his services, it could make for a sound way to get better in the future before his play potentially falls off.

articles.title: Are Steelers a real-deal Super Bowl contender after dismantling Browns for first place?
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have moved to the top of the AFC North following their decisive 27-6 victory over the surprising Cleveland Browns in Week 8. Th...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have moved to the top of the AFC North following their decisive 27-6 victory over the surprising Cleveland Browns in Week 8. The Steelers appear to be responding well to first-year coach Mike McCarthy. They have won their last four games, and they are going to have a chance to get some rest and rehab during their bye week before they face their most critical game of the season when they go on the road to play the explosive Cincinnati Bengals.

If Aaron Rodgers can make the critical plays in that game and the Steelers can come away with the victory, they should have the inside track on winning the division. However, gaining the division title is not why Rodgers returned for his final season or the reason that McCarthy took the job that had belonged to Mike Tomlin for so many years. This team wants to have a deep run in the playoffs and add to the franchise's legacy as a Super Bowl participant.

A good season to this point does not mean that the Steelers will become a dominant team in the playoffs. The bigger question is how will the Steelers compare to AFC powers including the Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots, Jacksonville Jaguars, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The answer has not been determined yet, but the Steelers are on the right track, and if they are going to play with the best teams in the AFC and beat them, they are going to need Rodgers to finish the year in a powerful fashion, they are going to need Jaylen Warren to continue to provide a solid running game and an explosive finish from disappointing WR D.K. Metcalf.

This is a difficult season for Rodgers, even if he is leading a first-place team. He made up his mind that he is retiring at the age of 43 (as of Dec. 2) when this season concludes, and that means that he is thinking of his life past football. Perhaps his concentration remains at a high level on GameDay, but a part of Rodgers is thinking about how much more comfortable life will be when he is not taking painful hits on an every-game basis.

Rodgers' numbers are quite good this season as he has completed 175 of 288 passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and 6 interceptions.

Rodgers has been sacked 23 times, but the success of Warren in the running game can take quite a bit of pressure off of the quarterback. Warren has 704 yards on the ground, he is averaging 5.9 yards per carry and has scored 7 touchdowns. Warren is clearly having the best season of his 5-year career. He rushed for 958 yards last year, and he should blow by that mark well before December.

Metcalf is the Steelers' big-play receiver, and McCarthy will need more from him as the season progresses. He has caught 33 passes for 378 yards with just 1 touchdown. Those are ordinary numbers and if the Steelers are going to beat the best teams in the AFC, he is going to have to pick up his level of play.

The big advantage that the Steelers passing game has going forward is the play of their tight ends. Huge Darnell Washington has caught 19-254-3 and fellow TE Pat Freiermuth has caught 25-235-4. Freiermuth is an outstanding red zone and third-down weapon, and the closer the Steelers get to the most critical games of the year, the greater his focus is likely to be.

T.J. Watt and the defense is capable of dominating

The Steelers have been more than solid on defense this season. They are allowing 18.0 points per game and that ranks fourth in the NFL. They also rank sixth in yards allowed and third in rushing yards allowed.

While this is not the famed Steel Curtain defense, this unit can put its imprint on any game. The key is the relentless pass rush of outside linebacker T.J. Watt. He has 7.5 sacks, 9.5 tackles for loss, 3 passes batted down, 1 interception, 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery.

Every great defense usually has that one dominant player who can set the tone, and Watt is that player for the Steelers.

He also has key teammates that also contributing to the defensive effort. Two of those teammates are linebackers Payton Wilson and Patrick Queen. Wilson leads the Steelers with 69 tackles and he also had 7 tackles for loss and 3 passes batted down. Queen has 60 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 4 passes batted down and 1 forced fumble.

Cornerback Jamel Dean is something of a secret weapon for the Steelers defense. He has 30 tackles, 8 passes defensed, 1 interception and 3 forced fumbles.

While Rodgers and the offense are clearly going to have to step up if the Steelers are going to prove themselves as Super Bowl contenders, the defense is going to have to make multiple statements. Watt & Co. look like a unit that could get even stronger when the season reaches its most crucial moments.

The Steelers are not Super Bowl contenders yet, but they have the ability to climb the mountain and get there.

articles.title: Chicago Bears deliver statement win over Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks as Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons star
articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons stars on his debut for the Chicago Bears against the Seattle Seahawks in his first appearance since arriving in a blockbuster trade from the Tennessee Titans; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs
articles.body:
Williams was extremely efficient for the Bears (6-2) against one of the NFL's stingiest defenses, committing no turnovers, taking just one sack and throwing for 247 yards while completing 71 per cent of his passes.

Williams' play helped set up three short touchdown runs by D'Andre Swift and that proved to be more than enough against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks (4-4), thanks to the impact Simmons had on the defense.

Acquired last week from Tennessee for a package that included two first-round picks, Simmons took little time to make a big impact on a defense that had lacked difference-makers.

He had a sack on the opening drive, added another tackle for loss and finished with six tackles and a pass defended as Chicago held Seattle to 252 yards and one third-down conversion on 11 attempts.

The defending champion Seahawks lost for the third time in four games and are now looking up at the NFC playoff standings and can ill afford many more slip-ups. The loss ended a 30-game streak for Seattle in the regular season and playoffs - the fourth longest for any team in the Super Bowl era - of not losing by more than four points.

Sam Darnold went 17 of 34 for 188 yards and two touchdowns for Seattle, but his interception in the fourth quarter set up Swift's third TD that made it 34-17 with 4:41 to play.

The Seahawks struggled once again to run the ball despite their trade last week for three-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and the return of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price from injures. Seattle ran for only 81 yards.

The Bears started off well against Seattle's stout defense by putting together a 17-play drive on the opening possession to take the lead when Williams threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden.

The Bears added two more field goals in the first half and built the lead to 20-9 in the third quarter with another efficient touchdown drive that ended with a 1-yard run by Swift.

The Seahawks were bottled up by Simmons and the Bears for almost the entire first half before Darnold connected with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on a 43-yard pass with 30 seconds left in the second quarter.

Things looked bleak for Seattle when Jason Myers had a 33-yard field goal blocked in the opening minute of the fourth quarter.

But DeMarcus Lawrence forced a fumble by Colston Loveland on the next possession that set up Darnold's 7-yard touchdown pass to Cooper Kupp, and Seattle converted the 2-point conversion to make it 20-17.

The Bears answered with another TD drive and put the game away after Darnold's interception.
